title: Vertex Cover, Independent Set and Koenig's Theorem
quickIdea: A vertex cover pays one vertex per edge, and in a bipartite graph its cheapest price equals the largest matching, which is Koenig's theorem.
remember: A vertex cover C touches every edge; alpha(G) is the size of the largest independent set and tau(G) the size of the smallest vertex cover.
Independent sets are exactly the complements of vertex covers, so alpha + tau = n for every graph.
The matching number nu is at most tau, because each edge of a matching needs its own cover vertex since matching edges share no endpoint.
Koenig: in a bipartite graph nu = tau, so a maximum matching and a minimum vertex cover have the same size; consequently alpha = n - nu there.
Koenig fails outside bipartite graphs: in a triangle nu = 1 but tau = 2.
A vertex of degree at least k+1 must lie in every vertex cover of size k, because leaving it out would force all its neighbours in.
A maximum matching in a bipartite graph is a maximum flow with unit capacities, and a minimum cover is read off the final level graph.

example.prompt: For K_{3,3} give nu, tau and alpha.
example.work: A matching has at most 3 edges and a1-b1, a2-b2, a3-b3 has 3, so nu = 3. K_{3,3} is bipartite, so tau = nu = 3 by Koenig, and indeed either whole side is a cover of size 3 while no 2 vertices touch all 9 edges. Finally alpha = 6 - 3 = 3.

gateAngle: Koenig turns a search into a count: in a bipartite graph you compute whichever of the matching or the cover is easier and read the other off. GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.37 tests the cover side, the fact that a high-degree vertex is forced into every minimum cover.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: For the 5-cycle give nu, tau and alpha.
variations.answer: nu = 2, tau = 3 and alpha = 2, and nu is less than tau because C_5 is not bipartite.
variations.why: Two disjoint edges fit but three cannot, while covering all five edges needs three vertices.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why can one vertex of a vertex cover cover at most one edge of a matching?
variations.answer: Because the edges of a matching are disjoint, so no vertex is an endpoint of two of them.
variations.why: That is exactly the injection that proves nu is at most tau in every graph.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A bipartite graph on 10 vertices has maximum matching of size 4. What are tau and alpha?
variations.why: Koenig gives the cover, and the complement of a minimum cover is a maximum independent set.

trap.what: Applying Koenig to a graph that is not bipartite, or using alpha = n - nu where nu is the matching number but treating it as if it were tau.
trap.why: Koenig's equality is a bipartite-only guarantee, and the identity alpha + tau = n uses the cover number, not the matching number.
trap.counterexample: The triangle has nu = 1 and tau = 2, so nu = tau fails, and its alpha = 1 while n - nu = 2, so alpha = n - nu fails as well.

check.question: A bipartite graph on 8 vertices has a minimum vertex cover of size 3. What are its maximum matching size and its independence number?
check.explanation: Koenig makes the maximum matching equal to the minimum cover, so nu = 3, and alpha = n - tau = 8 - 3 = 5 because the complement of a minimum cover is a maximum independent set.

sourceLine: Vertex cover, independent set, the alpha + tau identity and Koenig's theorem: GATE Overflow GO Classroom deck (English, read in part) for the independent-set bound and the complete-matching theorem; West for Koenig. Standard references used to verify, never copied: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications, ch. 10; West, Introduction to Graph Theory (Brooks, Dirac, Koenig, chromatic polynomial); CLRS ch. 22 (articulation points, bridges) and ch. 26 (bipartite matching); Diestel, Graph Theory (Menger). nu, tau and alpha are recomputed by brute force for every graph on up to 5 vertices and every bipartite graph on up to 6 vertices in scripts/validate.py, including the 2026 forced-vertex claim.
